target_customer: Operators of physical workplaces such as hotels, warehouses and restaurants, paid to supply task data to robotics labs and frontier AI developers
problem: Robotics and world-model labs need real-world task data, and workplaces hold it but have no way to capture and sell it. Sureform connects the two.
business_model: Data marketplace and collection service; revenue from selling captured data to AI labs
product_category: AI training data for robotics and world models

founders.name: Ananth Kashyap
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Previously: Penn, Google without saying which is education or employer, so neither field is filled.

technical_complexity.rationale: Time-synced capture of video, audio, pose, depth and tactile data from head cameras and grippers is hardware and data engineering, but not research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Access to workplaces could compound, but data collection services are copyable and labeling firms with large buyer relationships could enter.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later 2026 coverage shows Labelbox Prism, Mercor, micro1 and others buying operational data; no acquisition of Sureform found.

market_need_then: Robot foundation model and world model labs were hungry for real-world manipulation data in 2025, per the company's launch framing on its YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; the name is close to many unrelated Sure- companies (Surefyre, SureCheck) that crowd search results.

outcome_analysis: Sureform is an active small team from Spring 2025 collecting real-world human data for robotics labs. No funding, outcome event or traction figure was found in public sources, so no success or failure factors are assigned and the outlook is unknown.
notes: Company website fetch returned only a title. Team size is 4 on the YC page and 2 on a directory. No dated competitors near April 2025 were found; search results were from late 2026 so they are excluded from the list. YC page lists the founder as Previously: Penn, Google.
